lines.text: Is this the real New York or the one from the movies? It smells like the real one.
We walked here from Times Square. Our feet are filing a complaint.
Someone told me Queens is 'the new Brooklyn.' Brooklyn was the new Manhattan. Where does it end?
I asked a man for directions and he just said 'no.' Is that a local custom?
We came for the octopus. My husband came for the free bread. Both delivered.
The menu has a whole page of 'not on the menu.' I respect it.
Is it rude to take a picture of a pancake? I'm doing it anyway.
The man behind the counter sighed at me in three languages.
The cat on the bread is part of the experience, right? Right?
Everybody here is walking like they're late. Are they all late?
It's so hot the subway grates are breathing on me.
Our hotel lost power and the elevator guy said 'welcome to New York' like a threat.
Is that bridge famous? It looks famous. I'm going to tell everyone it's famous.
A man folded my pizza for me. Is that a tip situation? I tipped. I tipped a lot.
The sign says a dollar. My receipt disagrees. I'm keeping both as souvenirs.
Forty floors up and the waiter still sighed at me. New York is consistent.
We got caught in the rain and a stranger shared her umbrella and her whole life story.
There's a street fair. I've eaten four things on sticks. I can name two of them.
Wait, are you somebody? You walk like somebody.
Don't mind me, I'm just getting B-roll of my oat latte for the next forty minutes.
The lighting in here is giving 'struggling but make it aesthetic.'
I posted this place yesterday. You're welcome for the line.
I'm not an influencer, I'm a 'storyteller with a ring light.'
Do you think the plate smash would hit harder in slow motion? Asking for 80K people.
The arcade upstairs is SO retro. I'm calling it 'dad core.'
I asked for a 'deconstructed' bacon egg and cheese and Sal just looked at me until I left. Iconic content.
Golden hour on a rooftop is basically a second job.
Everyone's posting the brownout. Candlelight content is so saturated right now.
Wait, you're @ someone, right? You have main-character jawline.
A brand sent me forty free sweaters and now I can't feel my closet.
The restroom mirror here is the best one in Queens. That's a professional opinion.
The foam art here is a seven. My face in the foam would be a ten. Just saying.
Jojo wrote "Brinley" on my cup. My name is Brianna. I'm keeping it for the brand.
The sunset up here is free. The table is two hundred. Content is a business.
I come for the lighting. The DJ is a bonus. The drinks are a tax.
I've posted from four different queues tonight. Queue content is huge right now.
Sample sale week. I'm wearing three outfits at once so I don't have to carry bags.
You're new? Collab with me before you blow up. Lock in the early rate.
I don't drink coffee anymore. I drink a mushroom thing. It's going to be huge.
My Q4 is crushing it. Don't ask what Q4 means. I don't know either.
I moved to Queens for the value. I take a car back to Manhattan every night.
Not financial advice, but the lotto is a tax on people who aren't me.
This vest has seen things. Earnings calls. A wedding. Tonight.
Opa is just a high-five with ceramics. I'm in.
Bro, I networked so hard at the gym I forgot to lift.
Bottle service is an investment if you think about it. Don't think about it.
The market's down, which is a great time to buy a second vest.
Heard the Mayor's taking meetings in diners now. Very populist. Very bullish.
I don't spot, I mentor. The difference is I don't lift.
I tipped the host so hard he forgot my name. That's how you know it worked.
Mags won't take my metal card. She says the bar takes "normal money."
HR crackdown at the office. I had to take "rockstar" out of my email signature.
Ethics probe this week, so I'm only doing deals I can explain to my mother.
You run a business? Let's grab a protein shake and talk synergies. I'll expense yours.
Heard you're running a campaign. Need a donor who wants nothing? I want something.
I'm walking six dogs and one of them is emotionally running the group.
The pug is named Kevin. Kevin has a better apartment than me.
Billionaire's Pomeranian is having a rough week. I'm not allowed to say more. NDA.
I get paid in cash and in dogs looking at me like I'm the sun.
Sal lets me bring them in if they don't look at the bread. They always look at the bread.
It's too hot for the doodles. They're wearing shoes. Tiny dog shoes.
Rainy days the dogs come back looking like wet regret.
Every dog in Astoria knows which deli gives out ends of the turkey.
Morning walk is just me and the guy hosing the sidewalk. We nod. It's a relationship.
Sir Barksley's walker makes more than me and walks less. Respect, honestly.
Gus rates the dogs' form too. Kevin got a six. Kevin's upset about it.
Jojo gives the dogs a little cup of foam and charges me for it. Every time.
Arben saves the crusts for the dogs. The dogs know his schedule better than I do.
Sprinklers are on. Kevin has never been happier. Kevin is a pug in a raincoat.
Cold snap. All six dogs have better coats than me. One has a scarf.
You look like you need a dog. I can't give you one. I can let you hold a leash.
Twelve hours at St. Copay's and the first thing I want is pancakes. Don't judge.
Someone came in tonight because they 'felt a vibe.' The vibe was a pigeon.
You look tired. Drink water. That's free medical advice and the only free thing here.
I've been up for nineteen hours. Everything this diner makes is a miracle.
My breakfast is your dinner. My dinner is a coffee. It's fine.
Sal had my BEC ready before I walked in. That man is the real healthcare.
Heatwave nights are the busiest. Everyone's dehydrated and nobody believes it.
The generators kicked on during the brownout and I've never loved a machine more.
If you're dating someone in this city, check in on them. That's my medical opinion.
Arben stays open late enough for my lunch break. He's an essential worker to me.
Two slices at 1 AM isn't a nutrition plan. It's a coping plan. Different department.
Trains are down and half my shift is stuck on the N. We're running on vending machines.
Full precinct tonight. Half of them came to us after with "a headache." It was embarrassment.
Cold snap means everyone slips on the stairs. Wear real shoes. That's tonight's free advice.
Money doesn't fix sleep. Trust me, I've seen the rich ones at 4 AM.
DAD has held the Galaxy Gobbler record since 2019. We think DAD is a ghost.
I've been on level six for four years. Level six owes me money.
Respawn Arena wifi is faster than my life choices.
The claw machine is rigged. I've spent forty dollars proving it.
I streamed this pancake. Two viewers. One was my mom. Still counts.
Brownout means the arcade's down, so now I'm just a guy in a room.
If you beat DAD I'll follow you on everything.
Glow Up House hires people who are bad at games but good at yelling. I'm good at both.
Late-night arcade is the only place where everyone's equally bad.
The fridge is on the honor system. I haven't been honorable since 2021.
Cabinet three's record holder is twelve. He has a manager. The manager is his mom.
Friday tournament. I've been warming up my thumbs since Tuesday.
Power's out at the arena, so we played a board game. I won. It felt illegal.
Rain means every gamer in Brooklyn is in here. The air is forty percent energy drink.
You're kind of famous, right? Can I put you in my stream thumbnail? Shocked face, ideally.
Forty deliveries today. Thirty-nine said "leave it at the door." One said "come in." I did not.
My bike has more miles on it than my landlord has excuses.
Fifth-floor walk-up, no elevator, and the order was one soda. One.
I know every buzzer in Astoria. Half of them are broken. I know which half.
Tips are like the weather. Mostly bad, sometimes a miracle.
Rain means double orders and soggy fries. Everyone blames me for the fries.
Heatwave orders: ice, ice cream, iced coffee, a fan. Somebody ordered a fan. I delivered a fan.
Trains are down so everybody's ordering in. I'm basically the transit system today.
Arben gives riders the slices that come out a little too crispy. Best perk in the city.
Sal keeps a chair by the door for riders. He'll never admit it's for us.
Andreas tapes a note to every order: "Eat it hot or don't eat it."
Late-night orders are all cheese fries and apologies.
Morning orders are coffee for people who live above a coffee shop.
Delivered to a gym. He ordered a protein shake and a cheesecake. Balance.
I dropped off at the arena. Forty gamers, one pizza, zero eye contact.
You got a job? Respect. If they ever stop paying you, the bike's always hiring.
Broke too? Welcome. The free water at the deli is the best perk in Queens.
I'm not unemployed. I'm between callbacks. It's a different tax bracket.
I waited tables for six years and finally booked a role. I play a waiter.
Every conversation is an audition if you're brave enough.
I took a class on crying on command. Now I can't get through a commercial.
My headshot is from 2019. I'm aging into it. Slowly.
This dance floor is an audition nobody's casting.
Best acoustics in the club are right here. I warm up in this mirror every party.
Two slices and a soda: the official meal of off-off-off-Broadway.
I pick up shifts here between shows. Jojo says I over-commit to the name call.
The rooftop is gorgeous, but they asked me to stop doing my monologue at the railing.
Sunday matinee energy. Everyone's exhausted. Everyone's brilliant.
Every club is a stage tonight and I am every character.
Showtime season on the subway? I've been training for this my whole life.
Festival on Ditmars. I did a scene with a funnel cake vendor. He has range.
You're getting known. Can I play you in my one-person show? It's a short show.
You're dating someone? Tell me everything. I need material.
Late shows, later pizza, latest regrets. That's the life.
I've lived on this block since 1971. It's been "up and coming" the whole time.
My pension buys two coffees and one strong opinion a day.
Young people walk so fast. Where are they going? It's Astoria everywhere you go.
I don't text. If you want me, I'm on the bench. Gus is in my seat again.
Gus tells the 1987 story. I was there. That's not how it went.
Andreas's father ran this place before him. Same plates. Fewer of them smashed.
A slice was a quarter when I got here. Arben says the sign remembers.
I lift twice a week. The young men watch me. I let them learn.
Pancakes here every morning since they put up that sign. Lola tells me everything first.
Sal's father sold me a newspaper every day. Sal sells me a newspaper and a lecture.
Heatwave? We sat on the fire escape with a wet towel and we liked it.
Cold snap. I'm wearing three sweaters my wife knit. Three different decades.
Lotto fever again. I've played the same numbers since 1983. They owe me.
You're new? Learn the buses. The trains are for tourists and optimists.
A student? Good. Read everything. Believe half.
Morning walk, then the deli, then the bench. Some call it a rut. I call it a schedule.
We're like a dating app, but for laundromats. Pre-seed. Very pre.
I'm not unemployed. I'm in stealth mode.
Our burn rate is mostly oat milk.
My co-founder left to find himself. He found himself at a bigger company.
I don't have a desk. I have a café and a very long charger.
Table four is my office. Jojo charges rent in the form of one large cold brew an hour.
I pitched an investor here once. The bite was so small he forgot to say no.
We sponsor the Friday tournament. Our logo is on the trophy. The trophy is upside down.
I closed a round in a sauna once. I'm still not sure what I agreed to.
I came here to network. Mostly I've networked with the wall. It's loud.
Brownout took down our servers. Our servers are a laptop. The laptop is at four percent.
HR crackdown? We don't have HR. We have a vibe. The vibe is under review.
Every founder I know is suddenly very into compliance. Unrelated to the probe, they say.
You've got a crew? That's a community. That's a platform. Can I raise money on your crew?
You run a business? Founder to founder: how do you sleep? Asking for me.
Famous people make the best advisors. Want to be one? There's no pay. There's equity.
Morning standup is just me, standing up, in my kitchen.
My thesis is about the color of subway seats. My advisor is "concerned."
I paint what I see. Mostly I see rent.
Everything is art if you put a little card next to it.
My studio is my bedroom. My bedroom is also my roommate's bike storage.
I'm sketching the barista. Jojo keeps posing. It's ruining the authenticity.
The bridge at sunset is the most painted thing in Astoria. I paint it at noon. Counterculture.
Two slices: one for me, one for my still life. The still life never makes it.
The lighting in here is a gallery for bad decisions.
I did a whole series on the plate smash. It's called "Opa, Interrupted."
Sample sale week. I'm buying fabric by the pound and calling it a medium.
Rain is the best light in the city. Everything looks like it's sorry.
Festival week means free paint from the face-painting tent. Don't ask how.
Late night is when the good ideas come. The bad ones too. They look the same at 2 AM.
You're famous? Can I paint you? Not well. But often.
A student too? We're the backbone of this city's tote bag economy.
You've got a glow about you. I'd paint a little gold ring over your head. Very medieval.
I'm raising three kids. Two are my own. One belongs to his parents, technically.
The parents say no sugar. The grandparents say one cookie. I say what cookie.
This baby has a better schedule than I've had in my whole life.
The playground has politics. The Tuesday nannies don't talk to the Thursday nannies.
Twelve years in Astoria. I've raised half the kids who work the counter here now.
Jojo knows every stroller by name. She spells the babies' names wrong too.
Sir Barksley gets more security than the baby. The baby doesn't mind. The baby loves him.
Gus tells the kids about 1987. They don't know what a year is. They love it anyway.
Arben cuts the kids' slices into quarters. Tiny New Yorkers in training.
Rain day. Four kids, one apartment, one very long game of quiet coyote.
The sprinklers are on and every kid in Astoria is a fish.
The festival has face paint. By noon the baby is a tiger and I'm a tired tiger.
Morning drop-off is a military operation. With snacks.
You look like you need a nap and a snack. Everyone does. Ask anyone under five.
You're new? Learn which stations have elevators. It'll save your back and your faith.
You've got a crew? Good. Every grown-up needs a playdate.

places.text: Andreas threw out a critic once. Not his review. Him.
The bouzouki player knows four songs and they are all bangers.
Lunch rush in here is a contact sport. Elbows in.
The pancakes are shaped like the Hub sign. Nobody asked for that. Everybody loves it.
Lola's booth is reserved for whoever has the best gossip. You'll know when it's you.
Third stall's been 'on a call' for forty minutes.
Somebody wrote 'Tea is free, therapy isn't' on the mirror. Nobody's cleaned it.
The hand dryer here could launch a satellite.
Meatball the cat has bitten two health inspectors. Both passed the deli anyway.
Sal's coffee is a dollar. It's been a dollar since the Flushing Meteors were good.
Morning rush at Sal's is thirty hard hats and one guy ordering a matcha. Sal pretends not to hear him.
Everybody's in here because it's the only place with AC.
Somebody brought a candle and now it's 'a vibe.'
Jojo's tip jar has a label: "Film school. Or rent. Depends on the week."
The laptop row hasn't moved since Tuesday. One of them might be furniture now.
The morning line moves fast. The gossip moves faster.
Afternoons here are first dates and job interviews. Hard to tell which is which.
The chalkboard special is a "Rumor Latte." It's a regular latte. Jojo just likes the name.
The bass in here rearranges your organs. Nicely.
The bouncer turned away a prince once. He came back with a cousin. Also turned away.
Neon Nights: doors at ten, glow sticks by eleven, bad decisions by midnight.
Golden Hour on a weekend: sunglasses indoors and a DJ who says "afternoon energy."
Mags keeps a jar for everyone who says "do you know who I am." It's full.
The restroom line here has its own DJ. Nobody asked. Nobody's complaining.
Someone's crying in stall two, someone's fixing a lash, someone's on a work call. Classic.
This mirror has heard more confessions than the chapel on the corner.
A stranger just handed you a hair tie and a compliment. That's the club restroom code.
The bridge looks like a postcard. The joggers look like they're being chased by one.
The swim-cap lady turned away a city councilman last summer. He respects her now.
The morning tai chi crew is competitive. Don't stand where the man in white is landing.
Sunset over the river and every bench is a first date.
Sir Barksley has the shady bench. Nobody argues. He's been through enough.
The sign says a dollar. The sign has been lying, lovingly, since 2009.
Lunch line: hard hats, nurses and one guy in a suit pretending he eats like this.
A late slice tastes better. That's not science. That's Astoria.
Arben's daughter's soccer schedule is taped to the oven. The whole week runs on it.
There's a sign by the register: FORKS AVAILABLE ON REQUEST. DON'T.
The energy-drink fridge hums like a jet engine. People nap next to it on purpose.
Friday tournaments here are loud enough to register on the subway.
The top row of rigs is "reserved" by a sticky note that says ARCADE NERDS. It's binding.
Late at the arena, the screens are the only light and everyone talks in callouts.
Pixel's lost-and-found bin is ninety percent headphones and ten percent dignity.
Chalk dust, mirrors and men grunting in full sentences.
The front desk keeps very good records. Very good. Don't ask why that's a rumor.
The 6 AM regulars have trained together for years. They've never exchanged names.
Coach Bogdana's whistle can be heard from the L train.
Someone left a protein shake on the bench three days ago. It's a fixture now.
Forty floors up. The skyline does the talking. The bill does the shouting.
Thaddeus's waitlist runs "into next spring." It's November. He means it.
Sunset up here turns every phone into a tripod.
The plates are huge, the food is tiny and the food is incredible. Suspicious.
Late at the rooftop it's all deals being made and deals being regretted.

city.text: The N is running express, which means it's running wherever it wants.
Street fair on Ditmars this weekend. Six funnel cake stands, one porta-potty. Plan accordingly.
Rain like this, the bodega cats come out to judge us.
Lotto fever's back. My aunt bought twelve tickets and a vision board.
Cops are carding at every club door this week. Bring your real ID, not your vibe.
The Mayor cut a ribbon on a new ribbon-cutting ceremony. I'm not joking.
Somebody said the rent went up again. Somebody always says that. Somebody's always right.
Heard a celebrity's in Astoria this week. Everyone's wearing sunglasses indoors just in case.
You still working at that job? People are talking about your boss.
How's the campaign? Half this street has a yard sign and none of us have yards.
You and your person are the talk of the block. In a good way. Mostly.
Tell me you're not studying in here. Okay, study. I'll be quiet. I won't.
A hundred degrees. The pigeons are sitting in the shade like they pay rent.
Cold snap. Every radiator in Astoria is banging like it wants out.
Brownout on the block. The deli's running on a generator and Sal's personal grudge.
Sample sale on Steinway. A woman just fought me for a belt. Politely. With her eyes.
HR crackdown in every office in Court Square. Nobody's allowed to say "we're a family" anymore.
Ethics probe at City Hall. Suddenly nobody can remember who paid for lunch.
The 114½ is full tonight. Sgt. Bev is pouring coffee for the whole holding room.
Everyone's out tonight. Every club line in Queens is a block long and somehow fun.
Showtime season. Hold the pole and mind your hat.
Somebody painted a mural on 31st overnight. It's either art or a lease dispute.
Two people on my block are fighting over a parking spot. Neither of them owns a car.
Broke this week? The library's free, the park's free and the samples at Steinway Fresh are basically lunch.
Look at you, doing well. Don't forget us at the dollar slice.
Saw your crew at the Hub last night. Loud. The good kind of loud.
Heard your business is doing well. My cousin wants a job. My cousin wants every job.
People on the block say you're one of the good ones. Don't let it go to your head.
People say you know a guy. People say you are the guy. I didn't say anything.
Still single? Eight million people here and four of them are emotionally available.

lola.text: New in town? Cute. Stick with me and in a week the whole borough will be asking who you are.
First rule of Queens: never stand still on a subway stair. Second rule: tell me everything.
You've been here, what, three days? And you already have a regular order. I'm impressed. Barely.
People are starting to say your name. Not correctly, but they're saying it.
You're in that awkward middle bit. Too known to be nobody, not known enough to get a free table.
I heard you were at the taverna smashing plates. Good. Content.
Three people asked me about you today. I said 'who?' Keeps them hungry.
You're officially someone. Which means everyone's waiting for you to mess up. Don't. Or do, but call me first.
Oh look, it's the famous one. Sit. Not there. That's the gossip seat. Okay, sit there.
You used to need me. Now I need you. I hate it. Spill.
A job? Look at you, with a lanyard. I'll be gentle in my column.
Dating someone? Don't post them yet. Never post them first. Rule one.
A campaign. In this economy. I respect the delusion.
You've got a little halo glow. Careful, people love to see that slip.
I know what you've been up to with Pablo. Everyone knows. Nobody's saying. That's Queens.
Power's out, so I lit every candle I own. This is the best night the Hub's had all year.
It's a hundred degrees and somehow the tea is still hot. That's talent.
Morning gossip is the freshest. Sit, eat a pancake, I'll talk.
Late night is when the real stuff comes out. Order something and stay a while.
BREAKING: a new face in Astoria. Sources say it's you. Developing.
Pick a regular spot. Sal's, Jojo's, Arben's. People trust a face they see twice.
Quick tip: the dollar slice isn't a dollar and the free bread isn't free. Everything else, ask me.
Darling, nobody's famous on day one. Even I was new once. For about an hour.
Say yes to the next party invite. Sources tell me that's how everyone started.
Developing: your name came up at Velvet Static, in a sentence with "who is that." Progress.
You're trending in a group chat I'm in. Small chat. Big energy.
Insiders say you hit three places in one night. Hydrate, sweetie.
Rising is the dangerous part. Everyone's watching and nobody's protecting you. Except me.
Keep showing up. Stamps on a card become names on a wall. I've watched it happen.
On the record: you're one of three names people whisper in here. I won't say the other two.
Someone asked me if you're a real person or a marketing campaign. That's when you know.
Sources say you got the edge table at Altitude without a reservation. My inbox exploded.
Known is tricky. Fans give you free stuff. Fans also screenshot everything.
We reached out to you for comment. You never answered. Iconic. Do it again.
Your old order at Sal's has a fan account now. I run it. Kidding. Mostly.
Sources say a wannabe is copying your look. Badly. I'm told the shoes are wrong.
Fame manual: tip big, nod at the bouncer, never fight in a restroom. That's the whole thing.
Remember when nobody knew your name? I do. I was there. It's going in my memoir.
Everyone wants a piece of you. Give them a slice. A small one. Like Arben's.
You're the story now, darling. Write the next chapter somewhere I can see it.
Broke? Chile. Pick up a shift. Even legends pull espresso.
Money looks good on you. Tip like it. People remember tippers longer than outfits.
Your crew was in here last night. Loud, loyal, ordered the fries. I approve.
Sources say the dining hall has more drama than the Hub. Report back, student.
A business owner, signing paychecks. Check the register twice. I'm just saying.
Single? Good. Stay mysterious for a week. Then let me introduce you to someone.
Lotto fever's back. I don't play. I report on the people who play. Same thrill, no ticket.
Rainstorm. Everyone's inside and nobody can leave. Best gossip weather there is. Sit.
Every door in Queens is a block deep tonight, we're told. Pick one and commit.
Doors are tight this week. Bring your real ID, sweetie. The bouncers got new glasses.
Festival weekend. I've had four funnel cakes and twelve confessions. Busy day.
Afternoon lull. This is when the real regulars come in. Watch who sits where.
Evening. The booths fill up and the tea gets hotter. Pick one and keep your ears open.
